items.title: Direct integrals of unitary representations
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let G be a locally compact Hausdorff group and (X,𝔅,μ) a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space ([[def-standard-borel-space]], [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]), with a measurable complex Hilbert field having a countable fundamental family ([[def-measurable-hilbert-field-from-a-countable-fundamental-family]]). A measurable field of unitary representations is a family (π_x) such that every π_x is strongly continuous ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]) and x↦π_x(g) is weakly measurable for each fixed g ([[def-measurable-and-decomposable-operator-fields]]); the group identities hold for every x and every g,h. The decomposable operators π(g)=∫_X^⊕π_x(g)dμ(x) ([[thm-measurable-essentially-bounded-operator-fields-act-decomposably]]) define a group homomorphism G→U(𝓗), written π=∫_X^⊕π_xdμ(x) on the direct-integral Hilbert space ([[def-direct-integral-of-a-measurable-hilbert-field]], [[thm-direct-integrals-of-measurable-hilbert-fields-are-hilbert-spaces]]). This construction establishes unitarity and the group law; strong continuity of the integrated action is not asserted here. Changing the field on a μ-null set does not change any induced operator.
items.strategy: For each fixed g, the fibre operators are unitary, so their weakly measurable field is essentially bounded by 1 and defines a decomposable operator. The decomposable-operator theorem preserves adjoints and products. The pointwise identities at every x therefore give π(g)π(h)=π(gh), π(e)=I, and π(g)*=π(g^{-1}); hence every π(g) is unitary. The same theorem identifies fields equal off a null set. Pointwise fibre identities avoid any uncountable intersection of conull sets. Strong continuity is deferred to its separately assigned lemma.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through the direct-integral Hilbert-space supplier for completeness and through the decomposable-operator supplier for Hilbert adjoints. This definition makes no arbitrary field or conull-set choices.

items.title: Factor (primary) representations
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group and (π,H) a strongly continuous unitary representation on a nonzero Hilbert space. Set M:=π(G)″⊂B(H), the concrete double commutant, and Z(M):=M∩M′. The representation π is factorial, or primary, when Z(M)=C I_H; it is a factor representation when M is a factor. The commutants satisfy π(G)′=(π(G)″)′ by a direct consequence of their definitions. Irreducibility implies factoriality by Schur’s lemma. The converse fails: for every nontrivial ICC discrete group Γ, its left regular representation is factorial but not irreducible; a complete local argument is included in the item.
items.strategy: First realize ℓ²(Γ) as a Hilbert space by identifying it isometrically with L² of counting measure. For S=π(G), show S is *-closed, S'' is a concrete von Neumann algebra, and (S'')'=S'. Schur's lemma gives irreducible ⇒ M' is scalar ⇒ the center is scalar. For every nontrivial ICC discrete Γ, left and right translations show that a central z sends δ_e to a square-summable conjugacy-invariant vector, so z is scalar; a nonidentity right translation is a nonscalar commutant element, so λ is not irreducible. The finitary symmetric group on ℕ gives a concrete ICC witness. AC supplies adjoints, Schur's lemma, and L² completeness; the remaining group and conjugacy calculations use no further choice.

items.title: L1 of a second-countable locally compact group is separable
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group with a fixed left Haar measure $\mu$ ([[def-second-countable-space]], [[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]], [[def-complex-haar-lp-spaces-and-compactly-supported-functions]]). Then $L^1(G,\mu;\mathbb C)$ is a separable Banach space. There is a countable Borel algebra $\mathcal A_0$ generating the Borel sigma-algebra of $G$ such that the $\mathbb Q(i)$-linear span of $\{\mathbf 1_A:A\in\mathcal A_0,\ \mu(A)<\infty\}$ is dense in $L^1(G)$. Moreover, the image of $C_c(G;\mathbb C)$ in $L^1(G)$ contains a countable dense subset.
items.strategy: Use a relatively compact open cover and Lindelofness to build an increasing compact exhaustion. A countable algebra containing the exhaustion and a countable topological base generates the Borel sets. On each compact support, continuity gives a finite partition into Borel algebra cells on which the function has small oscillation; approximate one value per cell by Q(i) and choose the tolerance after fixing the finite Haar measure. This proves density of the finite Q(i)-span of finite-measure indicators. Countability gives a dense L1 family, and Countable Choice selects Cc approximants for a countable dense subset of the image of Cc.

items.title: Measurable fields of von Neumann algebras and their direct integrals
items.statement: Assume AC. Let (X,B,mu) be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space and (H_x,e_n(x)) a measurable complex Hilbert field with countable fundamental family. For every x let M_x be a unital concrete von Neumann algebra. The field is measurable if a sequence of weakly measurable operator fields generates M_x for almost every x. Define its direct integral as the set of induced decomposable operators from weakly measurable essentially bounded fields T_x in M_x almost everywhere. Define the diagonal algebra D from L-infinity scalar fields. The item proves D is a unital star-algebra included in the direct-integral set; it makes no weak-operator closure claim.
items.strategy: Use the direct-integral Hilbert theorem and the decomposable-operator theorem to interpret the set as bounded operators. For f in L-infinity, the scalar field f(x)I_Hx has measurable fundamental coefficients, is essentially bounded, and lies in each unital M_x, including zero fibres. Its induced action is M_f. Pointwise operations and the direct-integral pairing show D is a unital star-algebra, and changing f on a null set changes no operator.

No field or generating family is selected by this definition; the diagonal proof chooses one representative of one L-infinity class at a time.

items.title: Measurable Gram-Schmidt and constant-field trivializations on dimension strata
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space and let $(H_x,e_n(x))_{x\in X}$ be a measurable complex Hilbert field with countable fundamental family. Then: (1) there are measurable sections $f_n$ such that for every $x$ the nonzero $f_n(x)$ form a complete orthonormal system in $H_x$, and $x\mapsto\langle\xi(x),f_n(x)\rangle$ is Borel for every measurable section $\xi$; (2) for each $p\in\{1,2,\ldots\}\cup\{\infty\}$, the dimension stratum $X_p:=\{x:\dim H_x=p\}$ is Borel, and for every fixed separable Hilbert space $K_p$ of dimension $p$ there are unitaries $U_x:H_x\to K_p$ on $X_p$ such that $\xi$ is a measurable section on $X_p$ if and only if $x\mapsto U_x\xi(x)$ is a Borel map; explicitly, $U_x\xi$ has coordinates $\langle\xi(x),f_n(x)\rangle$ after deleting zero frame vectors; (3) weakly measurable operator fields have Borel transported matrix coefficients on each $X_p$, and uniformly bounded transported fields are Borel maps into their weak-operator-topology balls; (4) for every countable family of measurable sections $\xi_k$, the pointwise closed spans $S_x:=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\xi_k(x):k\ge1\}$ form a measurable closed Hilbert subfield, and its direct integral is the closed linear span in $\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$ of all square-integrable localizations $f\mathbf1_E\xi_k$, where $E=D_j\cap\{x:\|\xi_k(x)\|\le r\}$, $(D_j)$ is any countable finite-measure cover of $X$, $r\in\mathbb R$ with $r\ge1$, and $f$ is any bounded Borel scalar function supported in $E$. The zero-dimensional stratum is Borel as the complement of the positive and infinite-dimensional strata.
items.strategy: Apply measurable fibrewise Gram–Schmidt to the fundamental family and to the given sections. Count active frame vectors to obtain Borel dimension strata. On each stratum, map the active measurable frame to an enumerated orthonormal basis of a fixed separable Hilbert space; use a corrected countable rational-ball basis argument to prove the section criterion. For a countable family of sections, localize on finite-measure sets and bounded-norm pieces, test orthogonality with bounded Borel phases, and use the double-orthogonal-complement theorem to identify the closed span of the localizations with the direct integral of the pointwise closed spans. Real truncation radii reduce to integer radii by Archimedean cofinality. Finally express weak-operator coefficients in the transported bases and prove the WOT topology on each bounded ball is generated by its countable matrix coefficients.

items.title: Closed witness codings and completion measurability of Borel projections
items.statement: Assume AC. Let X and Y be standard Borel spaces with Polish presentations. Every Borel relation R subset X times Y is the projection of a closed F subset X times Y times N^N. For sigma-finite Borel mu on X, the projection onto X of every Borel subset of X times Y is measurable in the completion and differs from a Borel set only within a Borel mu-null set. More generally, every branch union of a decreasing Borel scheme indexed by finite sequences has that completion-measurability and Borel-version property. No global Borel selector is asserted.
items.strategy: Construct the Baire space N^N with a complete compatible first-difference ultrametric and an explicit countable basis. For finite Polish products, use bounded sum metrics, countable rational-ball bases, and locally prove the product Borel sigma-algebra equals the product sigma-algebra; this also verifies the standard-Borel product used in the statement. Code closed sets through N^N witnesses, close the coded class under countable unions/intersections, and obtain Borel closed witnesses. For finite Borel measures, construct minimal Borel envelopes of arbitrary subsets and use their null-difference property on a decreasing Borel scheme; outside the countable union of child defects, least-child recursion gives a branch. For closed projections, build nested rational-ball covers with shrinking diameters; branch intersections of projection closures are exactly the projection, by completeness and closedness. Disjointify a sigma-finite cover and assemble the finite-measure Borel versions and null sets. The source theorem on conull selection has its proof referred out; no selector is used or attributed here.

items.title: Measurable dense selections for fields of nonempty compact sets
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be a standard Borel space with a sigma-finite measure ([[def-standard-borel-space]], [[def-measure-space]], [[def-finite-sigma-finite-and-semifinite-measures]]). Let $(K,d)$ be a nonempty compact metric space ([[def-compact-space]], [[def-topological-space]], [[def-metric-space]], [[def-metric-topology]]) with a fixed dense sequence $(k_m)_{m\ge1}$, and give $K$ its Borel sigma-algebra ([[def-borel-sigma-algebra]]). Suppose $g:X\times K\to[0,\infty)$ has measurable sections $x\mapsto g(x,k)$ for each fixed $k$, continuous sections $k\mapsto g(x,k)$ for each fixed $x$, and nonempty zero sets $C_x:=\{k\in K:g(x,k)=0\}$ for every $x$. Then: (1) there is a sequence of measurable maps $s_j:X\to K$ such that $s_j(x)\in C_x$ for all $x,j$ and $(s_j(x))_{j\ge1}$ is dense in $C_x$ for every $x$; (2) for every $k\in K$, the function $x\mapsto d(k,C_x):=\inf_{c\in C_x}d(k,c)$ is measurable; and (3) for every open $U\subseteq K$, the hit set $\{x:C_x\cap U\ne\varnothing\}$ is measurable.
items.strategy: Prove measurability of closed-target hit sets by coding proximity and small function values on the fixed countable dense sequence. This gives measurable open hits and measurable distance functions. Recursively select the least dense-sequence point near each current zero fiber and intersect with a small closed ball; compactness yields a unique limit, whose measurability follows from a countable closed-ball criterion. Adding a nonnegative distance penalty restricts the zero set to each small ball, and the resulting countable family of measurable point selections is dense in every fiber.

items.title: The double commutant theorem for concrete von Neumann algebras
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a unital $*$-subalgebra closed in the weak operator topology. Then $M''=M$, and $M$ is also closed in the strong operator topology. Consequently the concrete von Neumann algebras of [[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]] are exactly the unital $*$-subalgebras that are closed in either of these topologies. For an arbitrary set $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ one has $W^*(\mathcal S)''=W^*(\mathcal S)$.
items.strategy: For a unital *-subalgebra A, use its diagonal action on a finite direct sum H^n. The closed orbit span of a tuple is reducing; its projection commutes with the diagonal action, and the projection blocks lie in A'. Thus every T in A'' sends each finite tuple into the orbit closure and is SOT-approximable. This proves the WOT/SOT closure equivalence and the bicommutant identity. Apply the same approximation to the unital *-algebra generated by S and compare its WOT closure with the WOT-closed bicommutant.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC. AC implies Countable Choice by thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice. Countable Choice is the exact premise for the closed-subspace orthogonal decomposition and Hilbert-adjoint suppliers, and hence for the orthogonal projection used in the finite-block argument. The concrete von Neumann algebra and general direct-sum interfaces also state AC. Their finite instances, and the individual approximant chosen for a fixed tuple and tolerance, require no further choice.

items.title: States, tracial states and faithful normal traces on a von Neumann algebra
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete von Neumann algebra on a complex Hilbert space $H$ ([[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]], [[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]). A complex-linear functional $\tau:M\to\mathbb C$ is **positive** if $\tau(P)\in[0,+\infty)$ for every positive operator $P\in M$ ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]), a **state** if it is positive and $\tau(I_H)=1$, **normal** if its restriction to the operator-norm unit ball of $M$ is continuous for the relative weak-operator topology ([[def-strong-and-weak-operator-topologies]], [[def-operator-norm]]), **tracial** if $\tau(ST)=\tau(TS)$ for all $S,T\in M$, and **faithful** if $\tau(T^*T)=0$ implies $T=0$. A **faithful normal tracial state** is a positive normalized trace that is both normal and faithful. In particular, $(M,\tau)$ is a **finite tracial von Neumann algebra** when $\tau$ is a faithful normal tracial state. If $H=\{0\}$ then $M=\{0\}$ and has no state, since $I_H=0$.

For a nonzero finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $K$, the normalized matrix trace $\operatorname{tr}_K/\dim K$ is a faithful normal tracial state on $\mathcal B(K)$, and it is the unique tracial state.

For a discrete group $\Gamma$ equipped with the discrete topology, let $H_\Gamma=\ell^2(\Gamma,\mathbb C)$, whose Hilbert-space structure under AC is established in the proof. Define the left and right regular operators by
$$
(\lambda_\Gamma(g)f)(h)=f(g^{-1}h),\qquad (\rho_\Gamma(g)f)(h)=f(hg)\qquad(g,h\in\Gamma).
$$
Put $L(\Gamma):=W^*(\lambda_\Gamma(\Gamma))$ using the concrete generated von Neumann algebra of [[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]]. Then
$$
\tau_\Gamma(T):=\langle T\delta_e,\delta_e\rangle\qquad(T\in L(\Gamma))
$$
is a faithful normal tracial state on $L(\Gamma)$.
items.strategy: Definitions plus local proofs. First prove the discrete group is LCH, establish counting measure as a Haar measure directly, and identify ell-two with complex L2 to get the Hilbert space under AC. Verify the finite-dimensional normalized trace with matrix units. For the group algebra, prove the left and right actions commute, verify positivity, normality, faithfulness, and traciality of the vector functional, extending the trace identity separately in both variables by WOT continuity.

items.title: Commensurator, unitary characters and monomial induced representations in the transversal model
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let G be a topological group and H≤G an open subgroup. (1) The commensurator Comm_G(H) consists of those g for which H∩g^{-1}Hg has finite index in both subgroups; it is a subgroup containing H. (2) A unitary character is a continuous homomorphism χ:H→T. (3) For a right transversal T with G=⊔_{t∈T}Ht and e∈T, write tg=α(t,g)(t·g) uniquely with α(t,g)∈H and t·g∈T. The formula (π(g)f)(t)=χ(α(t,g))f(t·g) defines the monomial induced representation on ℓ²(T); it is strongly continuous and δ_e is cyclic. If G is locally compact, this model is unitarily equivalent to the quotient covariant-function model and hence to standard unitary induction. If G is second-countable, T can be chosen countable and the representation is separable.
items.strategy: The transversal is selected using AC. Commensurability is a conjugation-invariant equivalence relation, so the usual composition and inverse calculations show Comm_G(H) is a subgroup. Uniqueness of the decomposition tg=α(t,g)(t·g) gives the right action and cocycle identities; these prove the representation law, and the right action permutes T while |χ|=1, proving unitarity. Openness of H and continuity of χ prove strong continuity on each basis vector near the identity; density of finite-support vectors and unitarity extend it to all vectors. The identity π(t^{-1})δ_e=δ_t proves cyclicity. For locally compact G, inversion identifies left cosets Ht with right cosets t^{-1}H; evaluation F↦(t↦F(t^{-1})) intertwines the covariant model with this formula after normalizing the discrete quotient measure to counting measure.

items.title: C star state GNS construction, purity and Polish pure-state spaces
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a complex C*-algebra and let $\phi$ be a state, meaning a positive bounded linear functional of norm one ([[def-c-star-algebra]], [[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]). There is a Hilbert space $H_\phi$, a bounded *-representation $\pi_\phi:A\to\mathcal B(H_\phi)$ ([[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]], [[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and a unit vector $\xi_\phi$ such that $\overline{\pi_\phi(A)\xi_\phi}=H_\phi$ and $\phi(a)=\langle\pi_\phi(a)\xi_\phi,\xi_\phi\rangle$ for every $a\in A$. This representation is nondegenerate, and any two such triples are related by a unique unitary intertwiner taking one cyclic vector to the other. If $A$ is separable, then $H_\phi$ is separable. A state is **pure** when it is an extreme point of the convex state space; a representation is **irreducible** when it has no closed invariant subspaces other than $\{0\}$ and its whole Hilbert space. The GNS representation is irreducible exactly when $\phi$ is pure.

Write $\pi_\phi(A)'$ for the bounded operators commuting with every $\pi_\phi(a)$. The assignment $T\mapsto\psi_T$, $\psi_T(a)=\langle\pi_\phi(a)T\xi_\phi,\xi_\phi\rangle$, is an order isomorphism from $\{T\in\pi_\phi(A)':0\le T\le I\}$ onto the bounded positive functionals $\psi$ satisfying $0\le\psi\le\phi$.

For separable $A$, the pure-state space with its weak-star topology is Polish. If $A$ is unital, its state space is weak-star compact and its pure states are exactly the extreme points; if $A$ is also separable, that state space is metrizable. If $A$ is nonunital, pure states correspond by restriction and unique state extension to the pure states of the minimal unitization other than its augmentation character; the corresponding state space of $A$ is the set of unitization states whose restriction has norm one, not all states other than the augmentation character.

For every nonzero positive $a\in A$ there is a pure state $\phi$ with $\phi(a)=\|a\|$. Hence every nonzero closed two-sided ideal $J\subseteq A$ is omitted by the kernel of some irreducible GNS representation; that kernel is a primitive ideal, meaning the kernel of an irreducible representation.
items.strategy: Construct the GNS space from the positive-functional null left ideal, prove left multiplication contractive, and complete. In the nonunital case establish positivity and state normalization of the unique unitization extension, identify its GNS space with the completion of A/L_phi via an approximate unit, and prove the restricted representation cyclic and nondegenerate. Match cyclic vectors for uniqueness and use a dense subset for separability. Realize every positive subfunctional by a bounded positive form and Riesz operator in the commutant, prove the converse and order equivalence, and connect purity to irreducibility through norm-additivity, reducing projections, and Schur's lemma. Banach-Alaoglu gives compactness for every unital state space; a countable dense test family gives metrizability when the algebra is separable. Midpoint images of separated state pairs show nonextreme states form an F_sigma, so pure states are G_delta and Polish. Prove the nonunital state and pure-state correspondences, including purity of the augmentation. Hahn-Banach extends a maximal-spectrum state to a positive norming state, and Krein-Milman gives a pure norming state; applying this to x*x detects every nonzero closed ideal.

items.title: A measurable direct integral of unitary representations is strongly continuous
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space, let $(H_x,e_n(x))_{x\in X}$ be a measurable complex Hilbert field with countable fundamental family and direct integral $\mathcal H=\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$, and let $(\pi_x)_{x\in X}$ be a measurable field of strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$ in the sense of [[def-direct-integral-of-unitary-representations]], with direct integral $\pi=\int_X^\oplus\pi_x\,d\mu(x)$. Then $g\mapsto\pi(g)$ is strongly continuous: whenever $g_k\to g$ in $G$, $\pi(g_k)\to\pi(g)$ in the strong operator topology. Equivalently, $\pi$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation of $G$ on $\mathcal H$ ([[def-strongly-continuous-unitary-representation]]).
items.strategy: This proves the strong-continuity sentence that the source states only as a citation to Dixmier's direct-integral theory ([Dixm-C*, Proposition 18.7.4]); the argument below is complete and quotes nothing unread. Fix $\xi\in\mathcal H$, viewed as a square-integrable measurable section, and a sequence $g_k\to g$ in $G$; second countability makes $G$ metrizable, so sequential continuity of $g\mapsto\pi(g)$ suffices. Every fibre is strongly continuous by hypothesis, so $\|\pi_x(g_k)\xi_x-\pi_x(g)\xi_x\|\to0$ for every $x$, and $$\|(\pi(g_k)-\pi(g))\xi\|^2=\int_X\|\pi_x(g_k)\xi_x-\pi_x(g)\xi_x\|^2\,d\mu(x).$$ For each fixed $k$ the integrand is measurable in $x$: the fields $x\mapsto\pi_x(g_k)$ and $x\mapsto\pi_x(g)$ are weakly measurable and $\xi$ is a measurable section, so all pointwise inner products involved are measurable ([[def-measurable-and-decomposable-operator-fields]], [[lem-measurable-sections-have-measurable-pointwise-inner-products]]). The integrand is dominated by $4\|\xi_x\|^2$, an integrable function independent of $k$, and it tends to $0$ pointwise, so the dominated convergence theorem gives $\|(\pi(g_k)-\pi(g))\xi\|\to0$. As $\xi$ was arbitrary, $\pi(g_k)\to\pi(g)$ strongly. Only the AC inherited from the direct-integral and measure-theory suppliers is used; the argument selects nothing.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the direct-integral and operator-field interfaces. It also implies Countable Choice, which is used with second countability (through first countability) to pass from sequential continuity of each orbit map to continuity. The dominated-convergence calculation makes no selections; the converse, continuity implying sequential continuity, is choice-free.

items.title: Conull Borel uniformizations and Borel versions of measured suprema
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space and let $Y$ be a standard Borel space. If $R\subseteq X\times Y$ is Borel and every vertical section $R_x:=\{y\in Y:(x,y)\in R\}$ is nonempty, then there is a Borel conull set $X_0\subseteq X$ and a Borel map $s:X_0\to Y$ such that $(x,s(x))\in R$ for every $x\in X_0$. For any such $R$ and any bounded real-valued Borel function $\varphi:X\times Y\to\mathbb R$, define $$m_{R,\varphi}(x):=\sup\{\varphi(x,y):y\in R_x\}.$$ For every rational $q$, the strict superlevel set $\{x:m_{R,\varphi}(x)>q\}$ is measurable in the completion of $\mu$, and there are a Borel function $\widetilde m:X\to\mathbb R$ and a Borel null set $N$ such that $\widetilde m=m_{R,\varphi}$ on $X\setminus N$. For any countable family of relations and scalar functions of these forms on the same measured base, the selectors and Borel versions may be restricted to one common Borel conull subset of $X$. A selector on every point of the original $X$ is not asserted.
items.strategy:
For each Borel relation, handle empty X directly. Otherwise pass to Polish presentations and use the closed-witness supplier to represent the relation by a closed F in X × (Y × N^N). The space Z = Y × N^N is Polish and nonempty. For scalar suprema, rational strict superlevels are projections of Borel relations, hence completion-measurable; choose Borel representatives and define a Borel version by the supremum of the represented rational levels.

For selectors, build a countable nested family of open balls in Z whose children cover each parent, whose closures stay in the parent, and whose diameters shrink. The projections P_s of F restricted to each ball are completion-measurable and each parent projection is the union of its child projections. Partition points by the least successful child, choose Borel representatives of all prefix cells, and remove the countable union of Borel null exceptions. On the remaining Borel conull set, the selected centers are Borel and converge. Countable Choice selects points of each closed fibre in the nested balls; their distance to the centers tends to zero, so the limit lies in the fibre. Prove the limit map Borel by testing preimages of closed sets with countable eventual-neighborhood conditions, then project to Y.

For a countable family of relations and scalar functions, repeat the selector construction and scalar-version construction for each input and remove the union of their Borel null exceptions. No selector on every point of the original X is claimed.

items.title: Type I factor representations and type I groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $H$ be a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space and let $M\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a concrete factor von Neumann algebra ([[def-factor-representation-and-primary-representation]]). A nonzero projection $p\in M$ is **minimal**, or **abelian**, when $pMp=\mathbb Cp$. The factor $M$ is of **type I** when it contains a nonzero minimal projection. A strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ of a topological group $G$ on a nonzero separable Hilbert space is a **type I factor representation** when its generated von Neumann algebra $\pi(G)''$ is a factor of type I; and a factor representation is of type I when it is a multiple of an irreducible representation (equivalently, by [[lem-separable-type-i-factors-are-multiples-of-irreducible-representations]], when $\pi(G)''$ contains a nonzero minimal projection). The group $G$ is **type I** when every factor representation of $G$ on a separable Hilbert space is of type I. The two descriptions of a type I factor representation agree: for a strongly continuous unitary representation $\pi$ on nonzero separable $H$ with $M=\pi(G)''$ a factor, $M$ contains a nonzero minimal projection if and only if there is an irreducible representation $\sigma$ of $G$ and $m\in\{1,2,\dots,\infty\}$ with $\pi\cong\sigma^{\oplus m}$ ([[lem-separable-type-i-factors-are-multiples-of-irreducible-representations]]); the standard defining equivalence with “all representations are type I” is recorded as an owner-held obligation of [[thm-equivalent-characterizations-of-second-countable-type-i-groups]].
items.strategy: Definition item. It records the minimal-projection criterion for type-I factors and the type-I group convention on separable factor representations. The statement's factor-type-I/multiple-of-irreducible equivalence is assigned to a later local lemma and remains an open supplier obligation; the all-representations group characterization remains owner-held.

items.title: Polar decomposition inside a von Neumann algebra and nonzero partial isometries between nonzero projections in a factor
items.statement: Assume AC. Let H be a complex Hilbert space and M⊆B(H) a concrete von Neumann algebra. If H=0, the polar clause is trivial and the factor clause has no nonzero projections. Otherwise projections mean self-adjoint idempotents, r≤p means rp=pr=r, and r,s are equivalent when w*w=r and ww*=s for some partial isometry w∈M; set pMq={pmq:m∈M}. Every x∈M has x=v|x| with |x|=(x*x)^(1/2)∈M and v∈M a partial isometry with initial and final projections onto (ker x)^⊥ and cl ran x. If M∩M'=C I and p,q∈M are nonzero projections, then pMq≠{0}; in particular nonzero subprojections of p and q are equivalent.
items.strategy: For x∈M, prove x*x positive, obtain its positive root through continuous functional calculus, and place that root in M because its generated C*-algebra lies in the SOT-closed algebra M; the root gives ker|x|=ker x. Define the polar isometry on ran|x|, extend to its closure, and set it to zero on ker x; verify its initial and final projections locally. The regularizers x(|x|+1/n I)^−1 converge strongly to this partial isometry, so SOT closure puts it in M. For the factor clause, L=cl span MqH is nonzero and reducing for M and M′, so its projection lies in M∩M′ and equals I. If pMq=0 then p annihilates L=H, a contradiction. Swap p,q and polar-decompose a nonzero element of qMp to obtain the stated equivalent nonzero subprojections; no family-wide choice is used.

items.title: The full group C star algebra of a second-countable group is separable
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, let
$q:L^1(G)\to C^*(G)$ be the canonical map, and let
$\mathbb Q(i)=\{a+ib:a,b\in\mathbb Q\}$. Then $C^*(G)$ is separable. More
precisely, there are a countable dense set $S\subseteq L^1(G)$ and a countable
set $D\subseteq C^*(G)$ such that $q(S)\subseteq D$, $D$ is closed under
addition, multiplication, adjunction, and multiplication by elements of
$\mathbb Q(i)$, and the $\mathbb Q(i)$-linear span of $D$ is norm-dense in
$C^*(G)$.
items.strategy: Choose a countable dense S; construct the countable coefficient field Q(i) using the rational-to-real and real-to-complex embeddings, and verify its closure. Form all finite Q(i)-linear combinations of words in q(S) and their adjoints. Canonical least-preimage indices and injective finite-sequence coding prove the expression set countable. The full-norm bound transfers density from S to q(L1), whose image is dense in C*(G). AC is inherited through the exact supplier assumptions; the local coding needs no further choices.

items.title: A sequential approximate identity concentrated near the identity
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group with left Haar measure $\mu$. There is a sequence $(u_n)_{n\ge1}\subseteq C_c(G)$ with $u_n\ge0$, $\int_Gu_n\,d\mu=1$, and with support eventually contained in every identity neighbourhood. It is a two-sided $L^1(G)$ approximate identity. If $q:L^1(G)\to C^*(G)$ is the canonical map and $\rho$ is a nondegenerate star-representation of $C^*(G)$, then $\rho(q(u_n))\to I$ strongly.
items.strategy: A local countability lemma lists the second-countable basis members containing the identity without choice, giving a decreasing cofinal neighbourhood sequence. Restrict the supplied normalized, support-concentrated $L^1$ approximate-identity net to that sequence; its directed convergence gives both $L^1$ limits. Since $C_c(G)$ is dense in $L^1(G)$ and the canonical map is continuous with dense image, $q(C_c(G))$ is dense in $C^*(G)$. Boundedness of the nondegenerate representation carries this density to a dense span of representation vectors. Multiplicativity reduces convergence on those vectors to the left $L^1$ limit; a uniform representation bound extends it to every vector.

items.title: Matrix-coefficient properties of the transversal model of a monomial representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a topological group; for i=1,2 let H_i≤G be open subgroups, χ_i unitary characters, and T_i right transversals for H_i\G containing e. Let π_i be the transversal representations on ℓ²(T_i). For a bounded intertwiner S:ℓ²(T_1)→ℓ²(T_2), put f=Sδ_e. Then f=0 iff S=0. If π_1=π_2 on one carrier, f is a scalar multiple of δ_e iff S is scalar. For every t∈T_2 and h∈H_1, χ_2(α_2(t,h))f(t·_2h)=χ_1(h)f(t). If t has infinite H_1-orbit then f(t)=0. If f(t)≠0 and t·_2h=t, then tht^{-1}∈H_2 and χ_1(h)=χ_2(tht^{-1}).
items.strategy: The preceding transversal definition gives the cyclic vector δ_e and the action/cocycle formula. If Sδ_e=0, intertwining makes S zero on the dense cyclic orbit; if the representations coincide and Sδ_e is scalar δ_e, the same argument makes S scalar. For h∈H_1, π_1(h)δ_e=χ_1(h)δ_e, so evaluating Sπ_1(h)δ_e=π_2(h)Sδ_e at t gives the coefficient identity. Its modulus is constant on each H_1-orbit. On an infinite orbit, an arbitrarily large finite subset would contribute n|f(t)|² to the ℓ² square sum, contradicting its finite norm. At a fixed coset with f(t)≠0, cancel f(t) in the coefficient identity and use th=α_2(t,h)t to obtain the stabilizer and character conclusions. AC is inherited from the transversal convention; the proof uses the given transversals and no further choice.

items.title: Free factors of the free group of rank two are self-commensurating with trivial conjugate intersections
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $F=\langle a,b\rangle$ be the free group on
$a,b$, given the discrete topology, and let $A=\langle a\rangle$ and
$B=\langle b\rangle$. Then $F=A*B$ is the free product of two infinite cyclic
groups,
$\operatorname{Comm}_F(A)=A$ and $\operatorname{Comm}_F(B)=B$, and for every
$g\in F$,
$$g^{-1}Bg\cap A=\{e\}\quad\text{and}\quad g^{-1}Ag\cap B=\{e\}.$$

Prove same-factor malnormality by retaining end B- or A-syllables under conjugation, and prove cross-factor intersections by universal-property retractions. Trivial intersections with an infinite cyclic subgroup have infinite index. Verify explicitly that the discrete topology makes F a topological group and A,B open before applying the commensurator definition.

items.title: Two common diagonalizations differ by a bimeasurable base isomorphism and a measurable field of unitaries
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(X,\mathcal B_X,\mu)$ and $(Y,\mathcal B_Y,\nu)$ be sigma-finite standard-Borel measure spaces, let $(H_x)$ and $(K_y)$ be measurable complex Hilbert fields with countable fundamental families and all fibres nonzero, and put
$$\mathcal H=\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x),\qquad \mathcal K=\int_Y^\oplus K_y\,d\nu(y).$$
Let $\mathcal D_X$ and $\mathcal D_Y$ be the respective algebras of scalar multiplication operators. If a unitary $W:\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ satisfies $W\mathcal D_XW^{-1}=\mathcal D_Y$, then there are conull Borel sets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$, a bimeasurable bijection $c:X_0\to Y_0$, and a measurable field of unitaries $u_x:H_x\to K_{c(x)}$ such that $\lambda:=c_*(\mu|_{X_0})$ is equivalent to $\nu|_{Y_0}$. If $r=d\lambda/d(\nu|_{Y_0})$ and $J:\int_{Y_0}^\oplus K_y\,d\lambda(y)\to\int_{Y_0}^\oplus K_y\,d\nu(y)$ is the square-root Radon–Nikodym unitary $(J\eta)(y)=\sqrt{r(y)}\,\eta(y)$, then
$$\bigl(J^{-1}W\xi\bigr)_{c(x)}=u_x\xi_x\qquad\text{for }\mu\text{-almost every }x\in X_0.$$
The diagonal-model identity is preserved, $WI_{\mathcal H}W^{-1}=I_{\mathcal K}$, and the implementing base map and fibre field are unique up to null-set modification.
items.strategy: Spatialize the measure-algebra isomorphism induced by W by coding both standard-Borel bases in [0,1], representing countably many rational cuts, and restricting the resulting Borel maps to inverse conull sets. Normalize the equivalent measure class with the square-root Radon–Nikodym multiplier, transport one field to the common base, and apply the decomposable-commutant theorem to a block unitary to obtain the fibre unitaries. Prove uniqueness by countable separation and fibre-field uniqueness; handle empty or zero-measure direct integrals explicitly.

items.title: Bounded density and finite-vector transitivity for C star representations
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space and let
$D\subseteq\mathcal B(H)$ be a nondegenerate concrete C*-algebra
([[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]],
[[def-c-star-algebra]], [[def-nondegenerate-star-representation-of-a-banach-star-algebra]]).
Set $M:=D''$ in the commutant convention of [[def-von-neumann-algebra-and-commutant]]. If $H=\{0\}$, the operator-density and transitivity clauses below
are trivial; assume $H\ne\{0\}$ for those clauses. Then:

1. $D_{\mathrm{sa}}$ is strongly dense in $M_{\mathrm{sa}}$, and the unit ball
   of $D$ is strongly dense in the unit ball of $M$.
2. If $M=\mathcal B(H)$, then every finite self-adjoint vector prescription
   compatible with a self-adjoint operator is realized exactly: for
   $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_n\in H$ and $c=c^*\in\mathcal B(H)$, there is
   $a=a^*\in D$ with $a\xi_j=c\xi_j$ for all $j$. If, in addition, finitely
   many orthonormal vectors are eigenvectors of $c$ with eigenvalues in a
   closed interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ containing $0$, include them in the
   prescribed tuple; the realizing $a$ can then be chosen with spectrum in $J$
   and with the same eigenvalues on those vectors.
3. If $M=\mathcal B(H)$, then for any unit vectors $\xi,\eta\in H$ there is a unitary $u$ in the
   minimal unitization $D^\sim$ ([[thm-minimal-c-star-unitization]]) whose
   represented operator sends $\xi$ to $z\eta$ for some $z\in\mathbb C$ with
   $|z|=1$. Here unitary has the usual C*-algebra meaning
   ([[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-elements-of-a-c-star-algebra]]),
   and $D^\sim=D$ when $D$ is unital and $D+\mathbb C I$ otherwise.

For a complex C*-algebra $A$, two pure states $\phi,\psi$ are called unitarily
equivalent here when $\psi=\phi\circ\operatorname{Ad}(u)$ for some unitary
$u\in U(A^\sim)$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(u)(a)=uau^*$ and $A^\sim=A$ when
$A$ is unital and its minimal unitization otherwise
([[thm-minimal-c-star-unitization]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-elements-of-a-c-star-algebra]]). Their GNS
representations are irreducible exactly when the states are pure
([[lem-c-star-state-gns-purity-and-polish-state-space]],
[[def-state-on-a-c-star-algebra]]). If their GNS representations are
inequivalent, then $\|\phi-\psi\|=2$. Orthogonal unit vectors in one
irreducible carrier likewise give vector states at distance $2$. Consequently,
if $\|\phi-\psi\|<2$, then $\phi$ and $\psi$ are unitarily equivalent.
items.strategy:
Use a positive contractive approximate unit and nondegeneracy to obtain strong convergence to the identity. Unitalize D and apply the finite-tuple bicommutant argument for strong density; symmetrize and use real Hahn–Banach on the finite-tuple image for self-adjoint density. Prove SOT continuity of C0(R) calculus through resolvents and Stone–Weierstrass, with vectorwise spectral-tail bounds; clipping gives the self-adjoint unit-ball result. Amplify locally to the block C*-algebra M2(D), prove its nondegeneracy and bicommutant M2(M), and compress to obtain full unit-ball density.

For exact finite-vector transitivity, project onto the closed finite-dimensional span, use its orthonormal basis, and extend the self-adjoint target by b=prp+(I−p)rp+pr(I−p), with norm at most 3||rp||. Explicit residuals are recursively corrected with geometrically shrinking errors; Dependent Choice selects the correction sequence and the norm-convergent self-adjoint sum gives exact action. Clip the result to a closed interval while fixing the specified eigenvalues.

For inequivalent pure GNS representations, prove the direct-sum image is nondegenerate and its commutant has scalar diagonal blocks and zero intertwiners. Bounded density separates the cyclic vector expectations by two, after passing to a self-adjoint quotient representative. The same transitivity gives norm distance two for orthogonal vector states. Below distance two, identify the GNS carriers, construct an internal unitary vector transport, lift its self-adjoint generator through the closed C*-image, and exponentiate in the minimal unitization.

items.title: A separable type I factor is a multiple of an irreducible representation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $M$ be a concrete type-I factor on a nonzero separable complex Hilbert space $H$. There is a finite or countably infinite exhaustive orthogonal family $(p_i)$ of minimal projections in $M$, equivalent to a fixed $p=p_{i_0}$, and partial isometries $t_i$ in $M$ with $t_i^*t_i=p$ and $t_it_i^*=p_i$. Put $E=\ell^2(I)$, $L=pH$. The unitary $W:E\otimes L\to H$, $W(\delta_i\otimes\eta)=t_i\eta$, satisfies $W^*MW=B(E)\otimes I_L$ and $W^*M'W=I_E\otimes B(L)$. If $\pi$ is a strongly continuous unitary representation of a topological group $G$ on $H$ and $\pi(G)''=M$, there is a strongly continuous irreducible representation $\sigma$ on $E$ with $W^*\pi(g)W=\sigma(g)\otimes I_L$, so $\pi$ is $\dim(L)$ copies of $\sigma$. Equivalently $N=M'$ is type I; a minimal $q$ in $N$ has invariant irreducible carrier $K=qH$, and an exhaustive orthogonal family $(q_i)$ of equivalent minimal projections in $N$ with $u_i^*u_i=q_i$ and $u_iu_i^*=q$ gives a unitary $V:H\to K^{\oplus m}$, $V\xi=(u_i\xi)$, $m=\text{number of }q_i$, intertwining $\pi$ with $m$ copies of $\pi|K$. The space $pH$ for a minimal $p$ in $M$ is the multiplicity space, not the irreducible carrier. In the direct-sum realization used here, the operators $\rho(A)(\eta_i)_{i\in I}:=(\sum_{j\in I}A_{ij}\eta_j)_{i\in I}$ for $A=(A_{ij})\in B(E)$ constitute the algebra written $B(E)\otimes I_L$, and $(I\star S)(\eta_i)_{i\in I}:=(S\eta_i)_{i\in I}$ for $S\in B(L)$ constitutes $I_E\otimes B(L)$.

items.title: Mackey-Shoda irreducibility criterion for monomial representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group, $H\le G$ an open subgroup and $\chi$ a unitary character of $H$. Assume that for every $g\in\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)\setminus H$ the restrictions of $\chi$ and of $\chi^g$ to $H\cap g^{-1}Hg$ do not coincide, where $\chi^g(h):=\chi(ghg^{-1})$. Then $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\chi$ is irreducible. In particular, if $H$ is open and $\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)=H$, then $\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\chi$ is irreducible for every unitary character $\chi$ of $H$; and if $N$ is an open normal subgroup and $\chi$ a unitary character of $N$, then $\operatorname{Ind}_N^G\chi$ is irreducible if and only if $\chi^g\neq\chi$ for every $g\in G\setminus N$.
items.strategy: By contraposition, as in Theorem 1.F.11 of the source. If $\pi=\operatorname{Ind}_H^G\chi$ is reducible there is a non-scalar intertwiner $S\in\operatorname{Hom}_G(\pi,\pi)$; by part (2) of [[lem-monomial-induced-representations-transversal-model-properties]] the vector $f=S\delta_e$ is not supported in $\{e\}$, while by part (4) its support is contained in the set of $t\in T$ with finite $H$-orbit. Pick $t\in T\setminus\{e\}$ with finite $H$-orbit and $f(t)\neq0$; then $t\in\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)\setminus H$. The adjoint computation $f'(t^*)=\chi(\alpha(t^*,t))f(t)$ for $t^*=e\cdot t^{-1}$ shows that $f'=S^*\delta_e$ is nonzero at $t^*$, so $t^*$ has finite $H$-orbit as well; applying part (5) with $t=t^*$ and $h$ in the stabiliser yields $\chi(h)=\chi(tht^{-1})$, i.e. $\chi$ and $\chi^t$ coincide on $H\cap t^{-1}Ht$, contradicting the hypothesis. The 'in particular' clauses are the specialisations $\operatorname{Comm}_G(H)=H$ (vacuous hypothesis) and the normal case, where the necessity direction is the same argument with the stabiliser described by conjugation.

items.title: Mackey-Shoda non-equivalence criterion for monomial representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group, $H_1,H_2\le G$ open subgroups and $\chi_1,\chi_2$ unitary characters of $H_1,H_2$. Assume that for every $g\in G$ such that $g^{-1}H_2g\cap H_1$ has finite index in both $g^{-1}H_2g$ and $H_1$, the restrictions of $\chi_2^g$ and $\chi_1$ to $g^{-1}H_2g\cap H_1$ do not coincide. Then $\operatorname{Ind}_{H_1}^G\chi_1$ and $\operatorname{Ind}_{H_2}^G\chi_2$ are not equivalent. In particular, if $g^{-1}H_2g\cap H_1$ has infinite index in $H_1$ for every $g\in G$ (for instance if it is trivial and $H_1$ is infinite), then the two monomial representations are inequivalent whenever $H_1\neq H_2$ up to the stated intersection pattern.
items.strategy: This is Theorem 1.F.16 of the source, proved by contraposition in the transversal model and fully reproduced there: if $\pi_1\cong\pi_2$ there is a nonzero intertwiner $S$, and $f:=S\delta_e\in\ell^2(T_2)$ is nonzero on some $t$ with finite $H_1$-orbit (parts (1) and (4) of the model lemma). Setting $t^*=e\cdot_1t^{-1}$ and using the adjoint $S^*$ together with the coefficient formula of part (5) shows that $tH_1t^{-1}\cap H_2$ has finite index in $H_2$ and that $\chi_1$ and $\chi_2^t$ coincide on $t^{-1}H_2t\cap H_1$, contradicting the hypothesis. The 'in particular' clause is the vacuous case of the hypothesis when every such intersection has infinite index (a group of infinite index is not of finite index), which holds for the free-group example used on the examples page.

items.title: Disintegration of a separable group representation over a commuting diagonal algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, $(\pi,H)$ a separable strongly continuous unitary representation, $A\subseteq\pi(G)'$ an abelian concrete von Neumann algebra, $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ a sigma-finite standard-Borel space with a measurable Hilbert field $(H_x,e_n(x))$ and direct integral $\mathcal H=\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$, and $U:H\to\mathcal H$ a unitary operator with $UAU^{-1}=\mathcal D$, the algebra of diagonalisable operators. Then there exist a measurable field $(\pi_x)_{x\in X}$ of strongly continuous unitary representations of $G$ on the fibres, defined for every $x$ by an arbitrary choice on a null set, such that for every $g\in G$ $$U\pi(g)U^{-1}=\int_X^\oplus\pi_x(g)\,d\mu(x),$$ and the field $x\mapsto\pi_x(G)''$ of von Neumann algebras generated by the fibres is a measurable field in the sense of [[def-measurable-field-of-von-neumann-algebras]]; moreover $\pi_x$ is nondegenerate for $\mu$-almost every $x$.
items.strategy: Transfer to the model: replacing $\pi$ by $U\pi U^{-1}$ we may assume $H=\mathcal H$, $A=\mathcal D$, hence $\pi(G)\subseteq\mathcal D'$ and every $\pi(a)$ $(a\in C^*(G))$ is decomposable, with a unique measurable essentially bounded fibre field $x\mapsto\rho_x(a)$ ([[thm-decomposable-operators-are-the-commutant-of-diagonal-multiplication]]). Choose a countable norm-dense rational-$*$ subalgebra $(a_k)$ of $C^*(G)$ (separable C*-algebra lemma). On the countable intersection of the conull sets on which the finitely many relations $T_{k+l}=T_k+T_l$ (rational scalars), $T_{kl}=T_kT_l$, $T_{k^*}=T_k^*$ hold, and on which $\|T_k(x)\Vert\le\|a_k\|$, the map $a_k\mapsto T_k(x)$ is a contractive $*$-homomorphism of a dense subalgebra; extend by norm continuity to a $*$-homomorphism $\rho_x:C^*(G)\to\mathcal B(H_x)$ with $\|\rho_x\Vert\le1$ (the extension is measurable in $x$ for each $a$, being a uniform limit of the measurable fields $x\mapsto\rho_x(a_k)$ along a sequence $a_k\to a$). Nondegeneracy almost everywhere: let $(u_n)$ be the sequential approximate identity of the previous lemma; the integrated operators satisfy $\rho(u_n)\to I$ strongly, and $\rho(u_n)=\int^\oplus\rho_x(u_n)\,d\mu$, so the fibre projections onto $\overline{\rho_x(C^*(G))H_x}$ converge strongly to $I$ in the integral and hence equal $I$ for almost every $x$ (dominated convergence for the squared norms against a countable fundamental family). Apply [[thm-nondegenerate-representations-of-c-star-g-are-unitary-representations-of-g]] fibrewise to obtain strongly continuous unitary representations $\pi_x$ of $G$ with $\rho_x(a)=\pi_x(a)$; measurability of $x\mapsto\pi_x(g)$ follows by writing $\pi_x(g)$ as the strong limit of $\rho_x(f_n)$ for a sequence $f_n\in L^1(G)$ forming an approximate identity at $g$ (matrix coefficients converge pointwise, hence the limit is measurable). Extend the field to all of $X$ by setting $\pi_x$ to be the trivial representation on $H_x$ off the conull set; the fibrewise identities hold everywhere by construction, so the definition of the direct integral applies and yields $U\pi(g)U^{-1}=\int^\oplus\pi_x(g)\,d\mu(x)$. The field of generated von Neumann algebras is generated by the measurable fields $x\mapsto\rho_x(a_k)$ almost everywhere, hence measurable. No operators are disintegrated separately over the uncountable index $G$, and no common null set over $G$ is used.

items.title: Measurable fields of von Neumann algebras have measurable commutants and centers
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(M_x)_{x\in X}$ be a measurable field of unital von Neumann algebras on a measurable Hilbert field $(H_x)$ with countable fundamental family over a sigma-finite standard-Borel measure space $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$, all fibres separable. Write $\mathcal M:=\int_X^\oplus M_x\,d\mu(x)$ for the direct integral. Then: (1) on a common conull Borel stratum there are WOT-dense countable measurable sections of the unit balls of M_x, M_x' and Z(M_x); in particular the commutant field $x\mapsto M_x'$ and the centre field $x\mapsto Z(M_x)=M_x\cap M_x'$ are measurable fields of von Neumann algebras; (2) $\mathcal M$ is a concrete von Neumann algebra on $\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$; (3) $\mathcal M'=\int_X^\oplus M_x'\,d\mu(x)$; (4) $Z(\mathcal M)=\int_X^\oplus Z(M_x)\,d\mu(x)$; and if two measurable fields of unital von Neumann algebras have the same direct integral, then they coincide almost everywhere.
items.strategy:
First work on constant nonzero Hilbert-dimension strata using measurable Gram-Schmidt; zero fibres are zero summands and are treated separately. The WOT operator unit ball B is compact metrizable: countably many basis matrix coefficients give a metric, and diagonal coordinate limits preserve the norm bound by finite-vector tests and reconstruct a bounded operator. Given measurable generating fields S_k for M_x, include their adjoints and normalize each by a positive constant essential bound, modifying a common Borel null set. For fixed x,T in B define g(x,T)=sum_{k,a,b}w_{k,a,b} min(1,|< (T S_k(x)-S_k(x)T)e_a,e_b >|), with positive summable weights. Each scalar coefficient is Borel jointly (coordinate sums) and WOT-continuous in T with x fixed; uniform convergence gives the same properties for g. It vanishes exactly on (M_x')_1. The compact continuous-zero-set selector yields a countable WOT-dense measurable family B_j(x) in this unit ball. Alternatively the conull selector selects on intersections with each countable basis open; either route gives precisely dense unit-ball sections, not just generators. Repeat with B_j and adjoints to obtain dense measurable sections of (M_x'')_1=(M_x)_1. For the CENTER use the simultaneous scalar coefficient equations commuting with every S_k and every B_j; their zero set in B is (M_x intersect M_x')_1, nonempty compact. Apply the same selector. An intersection is not generated by taking the union of generating sequences. The resulting dense unit-ball families generate the respective von Neumann algebras almost everywhere. The general conull-selection supplier also explicitly provides this basis-open density construction, without compactness of any projection graph.
For direct integrals, D is contained in integral M_x. Hence an operator in its commutant is decomposable by the published diagonal commutant theorem. Commuting with the countable bounded generators of M_x forces its fibre to belong to M_x' on one common conull set; the reverse implication is pointwise. Thus (integral M_x)'=integral M_x'. Apply this to the now-measurable commutant field and use the fibre double commutant theorem: integral M_x=(integral M_x')', so it is a concrete von Neumann algebra. The center identity follows by the two simultaneous fibre membership conditions. If two measurable algebra fields have the same integral, their bounded generating-field operators belong to the same integral and so belong fibrewise to both on one countable common conull set; the fields coincide there. This is an almost-everywhere assertion with the actual countable-field hypotheses, never selection at arbitrary discarded points.

items.title: Pure-state excision and density of faithful essential vector-state orbits
items.statement: Assume AC. A pure state of a unital C*-algebra is excised by a net of positive norm-one contractions taking value1 under the state. Sets {psi:psi(a)>1-epsilon} with positive norm-one a satisfying phi(a)=1 form a weak-star neighborhood basis at a pure phi. If pi is faithful irreducible and pi(A) intersects the compact operators trivially, then its pure vector states with vectors orthogonal to any fixed finite-dimensional subspace are weak-star dense in P(A). These statements transfer to nonunital A by unitization.
items.strategy:
Work first with a unital A. For a pure state phi let L={a:phi(a*a)=0}. Purity/GNS irreducibility gives ker(phi)=L+L*: for a in ker(phi), eta=pi(a)xi is orthogonal to xi; exact self-adjoint transitivity gives b with bxi=0 and beta=eta, so a=(a−ba)+ba, the first summand in L and the second in L*. The reverse inclusion is Cauchy–Schwarz.

Let J=L∩L*, a hereditary subalgebra, and e_lambda its positive contractive approximate identity. Put a_lambda=1−e_lambda. Then phi(a_lambda)=1, ||a_lambda||=1. If phi(b)1−b=c+d* with c,d∈L, then c*c and d*d lie in J; the approximate-unit estimate gives ||ca_lambda||→0 and ||a_lambda d*||→0. Hence

||a_lambda b a_lambda−phi(b)a_lambda²||→0.

The same proof can use the approximate identity on a directed finite-test index; no countability of its entire net is assumed. These positive contractions excise phi. For finitely many norm-one b, replacing a_lambda by its square (so its square root is the original a_lambda) and using state Cauchy–Schwarz shows that psi(a_lambda²)>1−epsilon forces psi(b) close to phi(b). Thus neighborhoods U_{a,epsilon}={psi:psi(a)>1−epsilon}, a positive norm-one with phi(a)=1, form a weak-star local basis at phi.

Let pi be faithful irreducible with pi(A)∩K(H)=0. Given a nonempty pure-state neighborhood choose such a positive a and epsilon. The spectral projection E_a((1−epsilon,1]) has infinite-dimensional range: otherwise (a−(1−epsilon))_+ is nonzero finite rank in pi(A), contradiction. For any specified finite-dimensional H0 choose a unit vector zeta in that spectral range orthogonal to H0. Its vector state belongs to the neighborhood. Thus the orbit of pi's vector states is weak-star dense in P(A), and remains dense while avoiding any finite-dimensional subspace of its carrier.

For nonunital A use the unique unital extension of a nondegenerate irreducible representation. If pi(A) has no compacts, neither does its unitization: a nonzero compact a+cI with c≠0 would make the injective Calkin image of A unital, so A itself would have a unit whose nondegenerate image is I, a contradiction. Pure states of A identify with the pure states of its unitization except the augmentation character. The needed neighborhood and orbit claims transfer. This avoids the source's noncyclic scalar spectral-model shortcut: only spectral projections and the finite-rank obstruction are needed.

items.title: Mackey Borel structure and countable separation of the unitary dual
items.statement: Assume AC. Let G be a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff group, and let H-hat be its unitary dual. For each finite or countably infinite cardinal n fix a Hilbert carrier H_n of dimension n, where dimension means the cardinality of a complete orthonormal basis. Give the irreducible strongly continuous representations on H_n weak uniform convergence on compact subsets. On their disjoint union with the sum topology, quotient the Borel sigma-algebra by unitary equivalence to define the Mackey Borel structure on H-hat. Every irreducible representation has a separable carrier by the local proof, so the quotient map is onto. A Borel space is countably separated when a countable family of Borel sets separates every pair of distinct points. No standard-Borel or pure-state-quotient identification is asserted.
items.strategy: Prove every irreducible representation of a second-countable group has separable carrier: a nonzero vector has dense linear orbit span, a countable dense subset of the group gives a countable dense orbit, and finite Q+iQ combinations are countable and dense. AC and its countable-choice consequence provide the separability, countability, and Hilbert Fourier inputs. Transport each individual irreducible to a fixed finite or countable carrier by orthonormal-basis Fourier maps, proving the quotient map is onto. Inverse images preserve complements and countable unions, so the quotient construction is a sigma-algebra; state the countable-separation definition without asserting the property.
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the unitary-dual set construction, fixes the countable family of carrier models, and implies AC_omega. Countable choice supplies second-countable separability, countable unions in the rational-span argument, and the Fourier-coefficient Hilbert isomorphisms. No family of irreducible representations is selected; carrier transport is done for one arbitrary class at a time.

items.title: Faithful essential pure-state orbits obstruct countable separation
items.statement: Assume AC. Let B be a separable primitive C*-algebra with a faithful irreducible representation containing no nonzero compact operators. Its faithful pure states form a nonempty Polish G-delta subspace F; every internal-unitary orbit in F is dense, meager and F-sigma. Every invariant Borel subset of F is meager or comeager; hence no countable invariant Borel family separates the orbits. There are inequivalent faithful irreducible representations of B. Consequently, if a separable A is not GCR, its primitive-kernel map is not injective and its Mackey dual ([[def-mackey-borel-structure-and-countable-separation]]) is not countably separated. Here GCR means every irreducible image contains nonzero compact operators.
items.strategy:
Suppose B is separable primitive and has a faithful irreducible representation with no compacts. All faithful irreducible representations of B then have no compacts: if one had a nonzero compact, its preimage would be a nonzero elementary ideal; restriction of any other faithful irreducible to this ideal is irreducible and nonzero, hence its image contains compacts by the elementary-ideal amplification supplier. This contradicts the assumed essential representation.

The pure-state space of a separable unital algebra is Polish. Its state space is compact metrizable by Banach–Alaoglu and a countable norm-dense test family. Non-extreme points form an F-sigma set: for each n take the compact set of pairs of states with metric distance≥1/n, map it by averaging, and take the union. Every nontrivial convex decomposition can be recentered as a midpoint of two distinct states. The pure states are the complementary G-delta. For nonunital algebras remove the augmentation character as above.

A countable family of nonzero ideals is cofinal among the nonzero ideals of B. Choose a countable dense family of positive contractions a_n and rational r>0; take nonzero c=(a_n−r)_+ and the ideals they generate. Given nonzero ideal J, approximate a positive norm-one element of J by a_n within epsilon<1/4 and take epsilon<r<1/2. Its quotient image has norm<r, so c∈J, while c≠0. Enumerate these nonzero c as c_k. For a pure state phi, its GNS representation is faithful iff for each k some b in a fixed countable norm-dense algebra has phi(b*c_k²b)>0. This is a countable intersection of open unions, so the faithful-pure-state subspace F is G-delta, nonempty and Polish. It contains every vector state of a faithful irreducible, and the preceding orbit-density argument shows that **every unitary orbit in F is dense**.

Each such orbit is F-sigma and meager in F. Fix its state phi and a countable norm-dense unitary family (u_j) in the unitization. It equals

union_j {psi∈F:||psi−phi∘Ad u_j||≤1}.

The closed balls are weak-star closed: the norm is the supremum of absolute evaluations on a countable dense unit ball. They lie inside the orbit by norm distance<2; every state in the orbit lies in some ball by approximation of its implementing unitary. Each ball has empty interior in F: in any nonempty neighborhood, the essential-orbit lemma chooses a pure vector state in the faithful representation of its center, orthogonal to the center's vector; its norm distance is2. Hence all balls are nowhere dense and the orbit is meager.

For any invariant Borel subset D of F, if D is nonmeager, its Baire property makes it comeager in some nonempty open U. Every orbit is dense, so the translates of U cover F; a countable subcover exists by second countability. Invariance and the homeomorphism action imply D is comeager on each translated U, hence on F. Thus every invariant Borel set is either meager or comeager.

If a countable invariant Borel family separated the orbits, choose for each member its comeager side (the set or its complement). Their intersection is comeager and nonempty by Baire, and all points in it have the same membership code, so it lies in one orbit. That orbit would be comeager, contradicting meagerness. Therefore the faithful-irreducible classes are not countably separated. Also they cannot comprise a single orbit, proving there are inequivalent **faithful** irreducibles of B.

Consequently, for any separable A failing GCR, choose an irreducible quotient B=A/J whose faithful image contains no compact operators. Pulling back the preceding conclusion proves both:

- the primitive-kernel map for A is not injective;
- its Mackey dual is not countably separated (restrict the assumed separating family to representations factoring through B and then to its faithful pure states).

This proves countably separated ⇒ GCR and injective-kernel ⇒ GCR without the omitted CAR-supported-state construction.
 Elementary-ideal link used here: a faithful irreducible pi with nonzero pi(A) intersect K(H) has all K(H) in its image. For its compact image ideal, finite-rank spectral cutoffs and a minimal-rank corner give a rank-one projection; irreducibility and multiplication by that projection give all rank-one operators, hence K(H). The preimage ideal is therefore elementary. Any other faithful irreducible restricts nontrivially to it. Its support projection, the strong limit of an approximate identity, is central in the generated factor, so restriction is nondegenerate and has the same commutant as the ambient representation. A representation of K(E) is E tensor L by its matrix-unit basis; irreducibility makes dim L=1. Thus the other representation also has compacts. This argument is local and does not use the Glimm implication being cited later.

items.title: Primitive ideals have standard Borel quotient-norm codings
items.statement: Assume AC. For a separable C*-algebra A, closed ideals are coded by bounded quotient C*-seminorms on a countable rational-complex dense star algebra. The proper primitive codes form a Borel subset of the compact metrizable code space, and this standard Borel structure equals the hull-kernel-topology Borel structure. Every closed prime ideal is primitive. The map from pure states to their primitive GNS kernels is continuous and open in this topology, and Prim(A) is Baire.
items.strategy:
Its topology is the approved hull-kernel/Fell topology. The map from pure states to primitive kernels is continuous and open. Continuity of a basic quotient-norm superlevel follows from

||pi_phi(a)||² = sup_b phi(b*a*a b)/phi(b*b),

where b ranges over a countable dense algebra and zero denominators are omitted. Each strict ratio inequality is open. Openness follows from excision: for any pure-state open neighborhood and any point in it, a smaller U_{a,epsilon} sits inside it; its kernel image is exactly {J:||a+J||>1−epsilon}, since any irreducible realizing J has pure vector states attaining the positive operator norm arbitrarily closely. Thus any open image is a union of basic kernel opens. The pure-state quotient induces the Fell/weak-containment topology by the existing RG-25 kernel convention, with the same quotient-norm basic opens. In particular, when the kernel map is bijective it is a homeomorphism, not merely a continuous bijection.

For completeness, primitive=prime for separable A can be proved here without citing Choquet. The pure-state space is Polish and its kernel map is open continuous surjective, so Prim(A) is Baire (pull back each dense open set). If A is prime, all opens corresponding to nonzero ideals are dense because any two nonzero ideals intersect nontrivially. Countably cofinal nonzero ideals are constructed here: choose dense positive contractions a_n and rational r>0 and retain nonzero c=(a_n-r)_+. For a nonzero ideal J choose positive b in J of norm1, approximate it by a_n within epsilon<1/4, and take epsilon<r<1/2. Its quotient image in A/J has norm<r, so c lies in J and is nonzero. The ideals generated by this countable family are cofinal. Each corresponding ideal open is nonempty by the norm-attaining pure-state supplier: a pure state detecting c has a primitive kernel not containing that ideal. These opens are dense when A is prime. They give a countable collection of dense opens; a primitive kernel avoiding all of them must be zero. Baire supplies such a kernel. Apply this argument to A/J to obtain closed prime ⇒ primitive. The converse follows from the factor-kernel proof using approximate units and the impossibility of two orthogonal nonzero central supports in an irreducible representation.

Code all closed ideals by the quotient seminorms q_J(a_n)=||a_n+J|| on a fixed countable rational-complex dense star algebra. The space of bounded C*-seminorms (including q(a*)=q(a)) on this algebra is a closed subset of the product of the intervals [0,||a_n||]: rational seminorm inequalities, product inequality and q(a*a)=q(a)² are countable closed conditions. Such a seminorm extends continuously to A. Its kernel is a closed ideal, and the induced injective star map from A/J to its seminorm completion is isometric, so it is exactly the quotient norm. Injective-star isometry follows directly from continuous functional calculus: a positive element whose image norm were smaller admits a nonzero spectral cutoff killed by the map. Thus the code space really parametrizes closed ideals and is compact metrizable.

Primitive codes form a **Borel** subset. Let a,b range over the countable dense algebra, and c over a countable norm-dense unit ball. A code is prime iff for every a,b,

sup_c q(a c b)=q(a)q(b).

If the quotient is primitive, bounded density in its faithful irreducible proves this equality by approximating the appropriate rank-one linker. Conversely a nonprime quotient has nonzero ideals with zero product; choose nonzero a,b from them and the equality fails. Continuity in a,b extends the countable tests to these arbitrary elements. The quotient image of the original unit ball is dense in the quotient unit ball by the definition of quotient norm, so the bounded linker tests genuinely exhaust all quotient contractions. The supremum condition is Borel by countability. Exclude the improper zero quotient. Thus Prim(A), using its quotient-norm coordinates, is standard Borel.

These coordinates generate exactly the topology-generated Borel structure: the superlevels {q_J(a)>r} are basic hull-kernel opens (use a positive cutoff), and other coordinate inverse intervals are countable Boolean combinations of superlevels. Conversely the basic hull-kernel opens are unions of these norm-test opens. This gives a genuine standard Borel model for Prim(A), not an assertion that every second-countable T0 space is automatically standard Borel.

items.title: Irreducible class and multiplicity of a type I factor representation are well defined
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a topological group, let $\sigma,\sigma'$ be irreducible strongly continuous unitary representations on nonzero separable Hilbert spaces $K,K'$, and let $m,m'\in\{1,2,\dots,\infty\}$. If $\sigma^{\oplus m}\cong(\sigma')^{\oplus m'}$, then $\sigma\cong\sigma'$ and $m=m'$. Consequently, if $\pi$ is a factor representation of $G$ whose generated von Neumann algebra is a type I factor, then the irreducible representation $\sigma$ and the multiplicity $m$ in any decomposition $\pi\cong\sigma^{\oplus m}$ are determined up to unitary equivalence by $\pi$ alone.
items.strategy: In the corrected amplification pi=sigma^{oplus m}, the commutant is B(l2(m)) tensor I_K: compute operator blocks and use Schur. An equivalence of two amplifications gives an isomorphism of these commutants. For finite m its complex algebra dimension is m^2, while the infinite case is infinite dimensional, so m=m'. A minimal projection in either commutant cuts out an invariant irreducible carrier, and any two minimal projections are equivalent within that commutant; the connecting partial isometry commutes with the representation and gives equivalent restrictions. Consequently sigma and sigma' have the same unitary class. This uses minimal projections in the commutant, not pH for minimal p in the generated algebra; that latter space is the multiplicity space.

items.title: Central disintegration: fibre commutant, centre and factoriality
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be a second-countable locally compact group, $(\pi,H)$ a separable strongly continuous unitary representation, and let $U:H\to\int_X^\oplus H_x\,d\mu(x)$ be a direct-integral model with diagonal algebra $\mathcal D$ such that $U Z(\pi(G)'')U^{-1}=\mathcal D$ (that is, $U$ diagonalises the centre). Put $M:=U\pi(G)''U^{-1}$. Then $\mathcal D\subseteq M\subseteq\mathcal D'$, and, for the measurable field of von Neumann algebras $x\mapsto M_x:=\pi_x(G)''$ generated by the disintegration $\pi=\int^\oplus\pi_x\,d\mu$ of [[lem-separable-group-c-star-representations-disintegrate-over-a-commuting-diagonal-algebra]], one has $$M=\int_X^\oplus M_x\,d\mu(x),\qquad M'=\int_X^\oplus M_x'\,d\mu(x),\qquad Z(M)=\int_X^\oplus Z(M_x)\,d\mu(x).$$ Consequently $Z(M_x)=\mathbb C I_{H_x}$ for almost every $x$, i.e. $\pi_x$ is a factor representation for almost every $x$; and if two measurable fields of unital von Neumann algebras have the same direct integral they agree almost everywhere, so the centre field is intrinsically determined.
items.strategy: Transfer to model D=Z(M), D subset M subset D'. Choose countable bounded generators A_n of M from the integrated C*(G) dense algebra, so their fibres generate exactly M_x. Choose countable bounded generators B_n of M'; because D subset M, these B_n are decomposable. On a common conull set B_n(x) commute with every A_j(x) and their adjoints. Any decomposable T with T_x in M_x therefore commutes with all B_n, so T in M''=M, proving integral M_x subset M. Conversely, the preceding lemma makes the field M_x' measurable and gives (integral M_x)'=integral M_x'. Every S in integral M_x' commutes with every A_n, hence S in M'. Taking commutants gives M=M'' subset (integral M_x')'=integral M_x by the proved double-commutant/field lemma. Hence equality. The commutant and center identities then follow from that lemma. Since integral Z(M_x)=D=integral CI and measurable fields with equal integrals agree almost everywhere, the centre fibres are scalar. This proof needs no claim that B_n(x) are fibrewise dense in M_x' and excludes the constant-trivial-field obstruction exactly by D subset M subset D'.

items.title: Compact groups are type I and their direct integrals collapse to discrete Hilbert sums
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a compact second-countable group. Then: (1) every factor representation of $K$ on a separable Hilbert space is a multiple of an irreducible representation, so $K$ is a type I group; and (2) every strongly continuous unitary representation of $K$ on a separable Hilbert space is a discrete orthogonal Hilbert sum of copies of irreducible representations, $$\pi\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha\in I}m_\alpha\,\pi_\alpha,\qquad m_\alpha\in\{1,2,\dots,\infty\},$$ over the countable set $I\subset\widehat K$ of irreducible classes occurring in $\pi$; in the Peter-Weyl case of the regular representation the multiplicities are the dimensions. In particular the continuous direct integrals of the general theory degenerate to atomic sums for compact groups.
items.strategy: By the published Peter-Weyl theory every unitary representation of $K$ is a direct sum of finite-dimensional irreducibles, equivalently a discrete isotypic decomposition $\pi\cong\bigoplus_\alpha m_\alpha\pi_\alpha$ ([[thm-arbitrary-unitary-representations-of-compact-groups-decompose-discretely]], [[thm-regular-representation-peter-weyl-decomposition]]); the set $I$ of occurring classes is countable because the nonzero isotypic components are pairwise orthogonal closed subspaces of the separable Hilbert space $H$. If $\pi$ is factorial, its generated von Neumann algebra is a factor, and the isotypic decomposition must have a single isotypic component, because the projections onto distinct isotypic components are central in $\pi(K)''$; hence $\pi\cong m\pi_\alpha$ is a multiple of an irreducible. Therefore every factor representation of $K$ is type I in the sense of [[def-type-i-factor-representation-and-type-i-group]], so $K$ is type I. Item (2) is the published discrete decomposition restated. The multiplicities for the regular representation are the dimensions of the irreducibles by the same published theorem.

items.title: Local analytic separation and saturated Borel quotient images
items.statement: Assume AC. Disjoint analytic subsets of a Polish presentation admit a Borel separator. A Borel surjection from pure states onto the standard primitive-ideal code space whose fibres are exactly unitary-equivalence classes sends every saturated Borel set to a Borel set. The quotient Borel structure of pure states agrees with the Mackey Borel structure ([[def-mackey-borel-structure-and-countable-separation]]) defined on irreducible-representation spaces, via explicit Borel GNS and vector-state maps. No late-page analytic supplier or global representative selector is used.
items.strategy:
The pure-state quotient and the usual irreducible-representation Mackey quotient have the same Borel structure. In one direction, a Borel field of irreducible representations with one fixed unit vector gives a Borel field of pure vector states. In the other, the GNS construction on a countable dense algebra has Gram coefficients phi(b*a), and the already proved measurable Gram–Schmidt/least-active-index construction produces Borel representation matrices on dimension strata. Therefore a class set has Borel inverse image in all representation spaces iff it has Borel inverse image in P(A). This is an explicit coefficient construction, not use of a global selector of irreducible classes.

The local closed-witness coding already commissioned on RG-26 makes images of Borel sets under Borel maps analytic by coding their Borel graphs. Repeat the following short separation proof rather than depending on the later analytic-separation page. Every nonempty analytic set is a continuous image of N^N: a closed witness is Polish, and nested complete-metric open covers give a continuous surjection from N^N onto any nonempty Polish space. For disjoint analytic A,B take such continuous parametrizations f,g. For prefixes s,t put A_s=f[N_s], B_t=g[N_t]. If all child pairs admit Borel separators C_nm, then union_n intersection_m C_nm separates their parents. If the original pair were inseparable, recursively choose a least inseparable child pair. Its two limit branches have distinct image points. Continuity gives disjoint open neighborhoods eventually containing their prefix images, a Borel separator, contradiction. AC chooses the countable family of child separators. Hence disjoint analytic sets have a Borel separator; analytic plus coanalytic implies Borel.

Under this lemma's stated hypothesis, the Borel surjection P(A)→Prim(A) has exactly the pure-state equivalence classes as its fibres. The lemma does not itself assert that GCR implies this hypothesis; the later GCR supplier proves the compact-ideal kernel injectivity before applying this conditional result. For any saturated Borel E⊆P(A), its image and complementary image are analytic in the standard code model for Prim(A); they are disjoint complements because the fibres are full equivalence classes. Separation makes the image Borel. Conversely every Borel subset of Prim(A) has Borel preimage. Thus the Mackey Borel structure is exactly the standard topology-generated Borel structure of Prim(A), transported by that class-bijection. The target primitive code is standard Borel and has a countable separating family, which therefore transfers to this quotient.
